📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that america's affordability crisis doesn't seem to be going away any time soon, with everyone's budgets getting battered left and right by inflation, record-high housing costs, war-driven fuel price hikes, and sky-high automobile operating costs. It's starting to feel a lot like the 2008 financial crisis out here in the streets again. I distinctly remember everyone suddenly caring about their fuel economy back then, scrambling for more fuel efficient cars. With new car prices higher than ever, that might not even be an option for you. So let's look into a few measures you can implement on any car to make it more efficient.

Obviously, the most fuel-efficient thing to do in a cash crunch is to drive less, take public transit, or get there without burning fuel on foot or by bicycle. If those aren't viable options for you, even the least efficient transportation machine can benefit from these five suggestions. And if you're getting 12 miles to the gallon right now, bumping that up to 13 or 15 could make a pretty significant difference to your weekly budget.

For example, at the current national average fuel price of $3.81 per gallon, a vehicle that gets 12 mpg combined and travels 15,000 miles a year (the EPA's annual estimate), would spend $4,762.50 a year on fuel, while bumping that to 15 MPG would mean spending $3,810 per year — that's a substantial annual savings.

In a recent development, here are five great ideas that you should definitely implement for your car to achieve better fuel economy. Some are more, um, involved than others, so before you dive into a project, make sure you have the necessary tools, skills, materials, time, space, and mental fortitude. You can absolutely do some of these projects yourself, but others might be best reserved for a professional, at which point you'll have to weigh the cost of modification against savings.

In a recent development, here in the United States, the midterm elections finished up, and if you live in a swing state, as I do, you were probably bombarded with political ads, and seemingly every yard had signage for an election campaign or a ballot measure. Most of those signs are made from a corrugated plastic material called coroplast, which is significant for its low weight and high strength. That combination makes them great for constructing your own DIY aerodynamic modifications. Getting the materials for free is just an added benefit.

Sources indicate that if you've been under a car before, you know that it's a lot less smooth than the shiny side you look at every day. There are exhaust pipes, suspension, driveshafts, and jacking points. If you manage to get a couple of the really big (and really obnoxious) yard signs, you could build a nice aerodynamically efficient flat floor tray for your car, improving the efficiency of airflow between the bottom of your car and the road. Tie it in to your rear bumper, and you'll help prevent a lot of turbulence.

Sources indicate that it should go without saying that your car's exhaust gets pretty hot under normal operation, hot enough to melt coroplast. You should build your flat floor in a way that the inexpensive plastic material is mounted far enough away from the exhaust to prevent melting, perhaps even with a heat shield material to protect the edges. It's also possible that political signs in your area aren't made of coroplast, so be careful when you're using unconfirmed plastic to block off your engine bay from airflow or releasing heat. To get a proper flat floor around the exhaust pipes, you can use sheet aluminum in hot spots to keep the airflow clean and prevent melting.

It has been revealed that after your flat floor, if you have some more coroplast laying around, you can build for yourself a grille block off. Because your car was built from the factory to operate in any temperature range, it has to have a larger grille opening and radiator than you need for light duty operation, particularly in the colder months.

Sources indicate that not only does selectively blocking airflow through the grille help improve the aerodynamic efficiency of your car at highway speeds, it will also help your car's engine warm up faster than it would with the radiator exposed to cold air. A cold engine consumes far more fuel than a warm one, so a faster warm-up time and maintaining heat within your engine compartment during trips with multiple stops is more beneficial to fuel economy than you might think.

You may have seen this sort of modification on diesel trucks and big rigs, especially in extremely cold temperatures. This is an easy one to get wrong, particularly if you forget you have a grille blockoff and leave it in through summer, so you'll have to pay attention to your car's gauges to avoid overheating. If you use them properly, you'll gain some winter MPGs. Again, it's important you know what you're doing with this project, as it is extremely easy to implement, but just as easy for it all to go awry.

Many automakers have employed expensive motorized grille shutters in an effort to improve efficiency. If you're really smart with electronics, you might even be able to craft your own motorized grille shutters with thermostatic controls that can potentially help improve your fuel economy in all seasons.

Chopping a section out of the middle of a car's height to lower the roof is a tried-and-true hot-rodding mod. While primarily used for looking cool, chopping the roof a few inches helps in many aspects of performance driving. Not only does it lower the car's center of gravity, but it reduces the frontal area of the vehicle, making it slip through the wind better. Improved aerodynamics are good for going fast, as your top speed improves, but it's also good for efficiency, as the car's overall aerodynamic drag goes down.

In the video above, the Motor Mythbusters made a dramatic chop to an old Dodge Tradesman van. Perhaps taking things to extremes is the best way to show their efficacy. It doesn't take a scientist to figure out that a Tradesman isn't very aerodynamic, isn't very fast, and isn't very efficient. By increasing its quarter-mile trap speed by several miles per hour, the team proved a chopped top was more aerodynamic.

It has been revealed that if you can cut through the air better, you need less power to maintain a normal highway speed, reducing your fuel consumption. If you want to get really wild with it, you can reduce your frontal area even more by making your car a single-seater and cut the greenhouse of the car in half down the middle, like this Geo Metro owner did.

Obviously, there are some practical downsides to chopping your roof. For one thing, it's hard to recommend cutting the structural pillars of your car, just for the effect it might have on the car's rollover safety. Modify at your own risk.

Sources indicate that bulky exterior mirrors are one of the areas where automakers have sought to reduce aerodynamic drag for decades. In order to comply with government safety regulations, the mirrors need to show what's happening behind you, and for a number of different seating positions, requiring them to be quite large and adjustable. As the owner of the car, you can theoretically modify your car with smaller aftermarket mirrors, reducing the frontal area of your car further than the factory could in the development phase. But what if you could get rid of your mirrors altogether?

Industry observers note that audi, a few years ago, introduced its "virtual mirror" technology on the old e-Tron SUV. It wasn't permitted for use in the U.S. market, but it did go on sale elsewhere. By swapping the giant mirrors for a compact camera on an arm, Audi claimed the reduction in drag (dropping the e-Tron's cD from 0.28 to 0.27) was good enough for a couple of percentage points in overall vehicle efficiency. The camera relayed exterior images to a small real-time video screen in each door. The system, while expensive, allowed Audi to bump the car's range numbers by four miles.

Sources indicate that because aftermarket modifications aren't mandated to follow the same strict regulations as OEM equipment, you could theoretically suction cup some GoPros on the outside of your car and have them relay the video via Bluetooth to your phone. Or, you know, you could do something a bit nicer and with less latency. Who wants a delay when you need to know if it's safe to merge? Maybe you could 3D print a little housing for a small lens and run some wire through the mirror hole to feed a dash-mounted video monitor? I've been looking into something like this for a future project of my own.

It has been revealed that weight is the enemy of efficiency, and modern cars have gotten quite heavy. The U.S. Department of Energy says carrying an extra 100 pounds of weight in your car can reduce your fuel economy by one percent. One side of that is to reduce as much of the cargo you're hauling around without needing to, so if you've been meaning to donate stuff to Goodwill and it's been in your trunk for a month, you've been taking a fuel economy hit as a result. On the other side, every pound of unnecessary weight you can remove from your car makes your car more efficient.

In a recent development, making your car lighter helps in every aspect of driving. A lighter car accelerates easier, meaning it'll require less fuel to gain speed at a given rate. It also means you can carry more speed through corners, reducing the need to brake and accelerate again. A lighter car is also easier on your consumable components, easing the efforts on brake pads and rotors, tires, and suspension components. An engine that isn't laboring quite as much will also wear less promptly and theoretically last longer.

So what can you do to reduce weight? I guess it depends on how much you can live without. A fully stripped interior with little more than a driver seat is going to be several hundred pounds lighter than one that's complete. If you can live without things like a center console, a stereo, a dashboard, and more, you could save a lot on fuel. If you want to be a little more pragmatic about it, there are still things you could do. You drive a minivan with a removable row of seats? You could save some fuel by removing those seats when you don't need them.

Did you always want to be a car designer when you grew up? Thanks to advances in 3D scanning technology, computer-aided design, computational fluid dynamics, additive construction, and instant-quote small-batch manufacturing, it's possible to design and build your own car's bodywork to your own exacting standards. Of course, you'll have to learn how to manipulate the software in order to make that happen, but it's definitely possible. Say you wanted to add an aerodynamic boat-tail or wheel skirts to your car, like the Volkswagen Mission Efficiency concept shown above. It's all within your reach!

A boattail shaped rear end is the most aerodynamically efficient way for a car to cut through the air. Not only does this allow air to continue to stay attached to the car, but it gives a smooth transition to clear air after the car goes through. An abrupt trunk with a blunt cutoff will create lots of turbulence behind it, which acts like a vacuum sucking the car's forward progress. By shrinking the low pressure area at the back of the car, there's much less pressure drag. Adding a five-foot boattail extension behind a semi-truck, for example, has been shown to increase fuel efficiency by almost twelve percent!

Sources indicate that similarly, wheel skirts help remove turbulent air from the car's trajectory through the air. Ecomodder logs show a few DIY wheel skirt projects with improvements from one to two miles per gallon, depending on application. Rear wheel skirts are much easier to install than fronts, as the front wheels need to exit the cover of the fender when turning, while the rear wheels are always covered. By filling in the gap between the fender and wheel, reducing drag, the car's engine doesn't have to work as hard to accelerate or maintain speed, improving economy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk, the chief executive of SpaceX and Tesla, said at the DealBook Summit recently that “the number of lives that have been saved” by Starlink connectivity “may be hundreds.”.

It has been revealed that want to get the correct numbers? Musk asked host Andrew Ross Sorkin, editor of DealBook, a daily business and policy report from The New York Times. “It’s all over the internet. Just do a search.”.

It was an ill-placed flippant comment, considering that Ukraine has suffered repeated disruptions to their access to Starshield — the military version of SpaceX’s Starlink.

In an editorial following President Donald J. Trump’s meeting this week with Russian President Putin and Chinese President Xi, former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton reminds readers that, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian access to US early warning intelligence about incoming Russian missile strikes has been fractured, and Ukraine’s access to Starshield’s service remains limited.

Starshield helps Ukraine shoot down Russian attack drones. Limited access to Starshield means increased Ukrainian deaths as the country battles against Russian aggression — the opposite of Musk’s broad brush claim of lives saved by his technology.

Musk did address restrictions on the Ukrainian military’s access to the SpaceX satellite communications network during the Deal book Summit. He mentioned that Starlink was never meant to be used for offensive strikes in war.

Historian and activist Rebecca Solnit refuses to dismiss Musk’s handling of Ukranian airspace as mere commerce. Elon Musk “has made much of his obscene pile of money off the US government with SpaceX and StarLink,” Solnit outlines. “They have given him power that should never belong to individuals – as demonstrated by his return to manipulating StarLink in ways that impair Ukrainian efforts in the war with Russia.”.

Representative Jim Himes (D-CT), the top-ranking Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, has written to Elon Musk with a formal request “that senior SpaceX officials meet with me to explain the Starshield service disruptions in Ukraine in October 2026.”.

Himes notes that SpaceX, Musk’s company, is “a US Government purchased service established via a contract between the U.S. Government and SpaceX.” Himes wants to know “why those changes were made, and whether those changes were made unilaterally by SpaceX or were directed by a US Government official.” Since SpaceX has potentially modified a US Government contract, “combined with its lack of responsiveness to congressional oversight,” Himes argues that “every contract the US Government has with Space X” should be questioned.

According to recent reports, reducing the controversy to everyday terms, Musk insisted during the DealBook Summit that the Starlink design is “revolutionary,” in that it can be placed on a roof. “It solves the problem of reaching people who are in a building.” Sure, gaps in service continue, but Musk has a solution. “The missing piece of the puzzle” to making Starlink ubiquitous is an alternative to a metal roof, he suggested. The solution is “terrestrial… we can establish micro-ground stations… a network that are, maybe, bound together with Starlink terminals. Instead of big cell towers all over the place.”.

Recent findings suggest that elon Musk is one of the richest people in the world, with significant political clout. He controls the direction and pace of one of the most important satellite technologies on which the US and the world depends, as former Secretary of Labor Robert Reich explains. Musk is one of the “authoritarians of the upcoming economy,” Reich encapsulates, and Musk has “unparalleled power over every aspect of the lives of Americans and millions of others around the world.”.

Reich adds, “The Democrats should investigate why Elon Musk funneled a half-billion dollars into the 2026 midterms. Was it because he wants to keep his satellite monopoly? His defense contracts?”.

Musk has a lot on his mind these days. Sorkin reminded Musk that he had once noted that his “mind was like a storm.”.

Musk responded that, right now, “I feel relatively at peace.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that if you guessed the startup Plug Power is in the mix, run right out and buy yourself a cigar.
  • It has been revealed that plug Power soon pivoted into replacing gas-derived hydrogen fuel with so-named green hydrogen, pushed from water by an electrical current.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When US President Donald Trump swept into office last year, he set his choppers upon the $8 billion Regional Clean Hydrogen Hubs program, snuffing out plans to establish a diversified, domestic hydrogen market with a focus on decarbonization. Nevertheless, some stakeholders have continued to pursue the dream of producing green hydrogen from renewable resources — instead of squeezing it from natural gas. Now all that hard work is beginning to pay off, Trump or no Trump.

It has been revealed that if you guessed the startup Plug Power is in the mix, run right out and buy yourself a cigar. Plug Power began life back in 1997 with a focus on electric forklifts powered by zero emission hydrogen fuel cells. In addition to replacing fossil fuels, Plug Power aimed to replace battery-powered forklifts, with fuel cells being a better fit for the fast-paced environment of shipping and logistics.

It has been revealed that plug Power soon pivoted into replacing gas-derived hydrogen fuel with so-named green hydrogen, pushed from water by an electrical current. After a series of ups and downs the company hit the jackpot in January of 2025, when the US Department of Energy tapped it for a $1.66 loan guarantee in support of the Regional Clean Hydrogen Hubs program, which was funded through the 2021 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. If all went according to initiative, Plug Power would have used the loan to finance up to six green hydrogen projects around the US, all affiliated with the Hydrogen Hubs program.

It has been revealed that so much for that. The Energy Department declared the loan award at the beginning of the month, when former President Joe Biden was still in office. However, by the end of the month Trump was officially installed in the White House. He soon pulled the plug on the Plug Power loan, so to speak, sending it down the drain alongside many other federally funded clean power projects.

Industry observers note that that was not the end of the story for Plug Power. After all, it’s a major world out there, and Plug Power continued to pitch its wares overseas. Last week the company also relaunched itself back into the US market, bigly.

It has been revealed that on November 17, Plug Power unveiled that its newly introduced “GenEco™ Scale” green hydrogen electrolyzer system is up for grabs in the US market while concurrently announcing that its first customer is the Texas-based firm Aracdia eFuels. Arcadia will deploy 280 megawatts’ worth of GenEco Scale modules at its Project ARC campus in the Portland/Corpus Christi area in Texas. When fully up and running, Project ARC will deploy green hydrogen from the GenEco Scale system to produce about 23.2 million gallons of fossil-free aviation fuel per year.

While green hydrogen has its fans in the decarbonization field, the stubbornly high cost of electrolysis has raised a formidable obstacle against widespread commercial uptake. Plug Power is among the stakeholders pitching modular, integrated systems to help bring costs down into parity with conventional hydrogen sourced from natural gas or coal, and that’s where the GenEco system comes into play.

Industry observers note that “Built around a standardized 20 MW block architecture, GenEco Scale combines Plug’s proven proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer technology with integrated balance-of-plant systems into a modular, pre-engineered solution for hydrogen production projects of approximately 100 MW and above,” Plug Power explained in a press statement last week. The company also noted that the “outdoor-ready” system avoids much of the cost and time related to the buildings and other infrastructure required of traditional large scale electrolyzer systems.

Arcadia eFuels CEO Amy Hebert also chipped in her two cents in support of the modular system. “Reducing the engineering burden on our EPC [engineering, procurement, and construction] partners and minimizing the complexity of bringing these systems together were important considerations for Project ARC,” Herbert emphasized.

Sources indicate that savings on land is another part of the cost-cutting blueprint. Unlike conventional electrolyzer system layouts, the GenEco model deploys a vertical configuration. The vertical system requires less than one acre per 100 megawatts of electrolyzer capacity, according to Plug Power.

Another Plug Power project has bubbled up in California, which was on track to host a suite of projects under the Hydrogen Hubs program with a focus on hydrogen derived from biomass as well as water electrolysis. The funding evaporated under Trump, but the state is still getting its hands on green hydrogen.

On November 19, Plug Power announced that its containerized 5-megawatt GenEco electrolyzer is up and running at a green hydrogen plant in Vernon, California, under the umbrella of the Fresh Jersey-based firm Avina Clean Hydrogen.

Green hydrogen from this project will go to fulfill California’s plans for a zero-emission freight corridor, the plan for which includes fuel cell electric trucks as well as battery-powered trucks. “Located approximately 10 miles from the Port of Long Beach, the facility is designed to serve fleets moving freight through the Los Angeles–Long Beach port complex. It combines on-site fueling with tube-trailer deliveries to customers across the Los Angeles region,” Plug Power explains.

In a recent development, the station, also accommodate buses, and it can refuel a heavy-duty vehicle to more than 95% capacity in less than 30 minutes, according to Plug Power. That stacks up well against charging times for battery-powered heavy duty vehicles. On its website, for example, Tesla asserts that its latest Semi electric truck can recover 60% of its 500 mile range in up to 30 minutes at a Tesla Megacharger station.

For the record, Avina has not placed all of its cards on hydrogen fuel cell trucks. The organization’s roster of clean hydrogen projects also includes SAF (sustainable aviation fuel) and green ammonia, which is a key input for fertilizer among other chemical products.

Rounding out the trio of fresh projects is the Swedish firm PowerCell Group. The firm is better known for its work in the marine energy field, and now it is tapping into land-based markets as well. Last week PowerCell revealed that its US branch is in motion to set up a green hydrogen system run by excess electricity from an existing solar array owned by a to-be-named client in the US. In effect, the hydrogen will serve as an energy storage medium. It will go to run a PowerCell PowerPod 3000 stationary fuel cell, which will kick into action at night to keep the clean kilowatts flowing after the sun goes down.

PowerCell describes the PowerPod 3000 as “a containerized power generation platform integrating our PS190 systems with power conversion equipment, cooling and DMC, PowerCell’s control and Energy Orchestration technology,” with an installed fuel cell capacity of 27 megawatts and 20 megawatts of rated power.

Recent findings suggest that that’s a good question. Rather than let that excess solar electricity go to waste, the client could invest in a BESS (battery energy storage system) for daytime energy storage and night-time electricity. However, a typical BESS only lasts for a handful of hours. In contrast, PowerCell describes its fuel cell as a “long duration” storage system, which generally means eight hours or more.

PowerCell also points out that a fuel cell does something that a BESS cannot. Fuel cells generate electricity by combining hydrogen with oxygen in the presence of a catalyst. Water — H2O — is a byproduct. All else being equal, that opens up the potential for green hydrogen to serve as a water distribution medium, sucking up water in an electrolysis system at one location, then pushing it out in a fuel cell located elsewhere.

PowerCell is not making any specific promises for this particular project, though the manufacturer does emphasize that “the ability to generate both electricity and recoverable water adds another dimension of value to hydrogen-based energy storage.”.

“The amount of water recovered, and its potential uses will depend on the final system configuration, operating conditions and water treatment requirements,” the tech giant adds.

Recent findings suggest that and, that’s where things get interesting. The client is a to-be-named electric cooperative, which is of interest because electric cooperatives (more specifically, Rural Electric Cooperatives) account for a large portion of the US grid, and their roots in the rural poverty fighting programs of the Great Depression provide for a distinctive public benefit mission that can, in some cases, allow more wiggle room for innovative energy solutions that generate broad benefits for local communities.

Recent findings suggest that I’m reaching out to PowerCell for more details. If they can’t divulge the name of the client yet, perhaps they’ll be able to describe what they mean by long duration energy storage, so stay tuned for an update.

Court Bars BYD Ti7 From Sale In Europe For Looking Way Too Much Like A Land Rover Defender

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (521 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that china's BYD is now officially barred from selling its Ti7 SUV in Europe because a Dutch district court in The Hague ruled that it looked far too much like the Land Rover Defender.
  • Although it has been on sale in China since last year, JLR released the case earlier this year after BYD announced on its UK website that the seven-seater would be available to order, with customer deliveries starting in January of 2027, according to Reuters.
  • Sources indicate that the injunction against BYD will take effect a week after the ruling since the automaker "currently has no concrete plans to place the Ti7 on the market in the EU," according to Reuters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that china's BYD is now officially barred from selling its Ti7 SUV in Europe because a Dutch district court in The Hague ruled that it looked far too much like the Land Rover Defender. While it's certainly not a one-to-one copy, I can certainly see why the folks over at Jaguar-Land Rover's legal department would be a bit miffed.

Although it has been on sale in China since last year, JLR released the case earlier this year after BYD announced on its UK website that the seven-seater would be available to order, with customer deliveries starting in January of 2027, according to Reuters. Now, there's an injunction against its sale in the EU. The one caveat of all of this is that this court in the Netherlands has no jurisdiction over BYD's affiliate in the UK.

Sources indicate that the injunction against BYD will take effect a week after the ruling since the automaker "currently has no concrete plans to place the Ti7 on the market in the EU," according to Reuters. Until the whole intellectual property case is resolved, the court is banning BYD from producing the — admittedly good-looking — vehicle at its fresh factory in Hungary. It's due to spin up mass production of other vehicles next year, but the Ti7 will not be one of them unless something drastic changes very quickly.

Industry observers note that "In these summary proceedings, the preliminary relief judge rules that ​the Ti7 infringes the EU design of Jaguar Land Rover," Reuters reports the court ruling said. "The characteristic ⁠and distinctive elements of the design are reflected in the BYD Ti7.".

Sources indicate that some of the more notable visual similarities are the boxy, flat-roof silhouette, its upright proportions, its side-hinged tailgate and squared-off wheel arches. The real kicker has to be the solid body-colored panel behind the rear passenger door, which is controversial on the Defender, yet BYD designers decided to include it anyway.

It has been revealed that it's actually fairly rare in Europe for a large automaker to go to court over design rights infringement. It's also uncommon for a ruling to come down so early in proceedings for a case that is ongoing and likely to last some time. JLR, of course, is pleased with the outcome, telling Reuters, "We protect our intellectual property and take legal action when necessary.".

Still, this isn't exactly the first  time something like this has happened, as Reuters explains:.

Industry observers note that legacy automakers ​have often complained that ⁠Chinese automakers have copied designs, though little has been proven in court. In 2005, for instance, General Motors and Chinese rival Chery settled a case over the Chery QQ ​that the No. 1 US automaker said was a copy of its Chevrolet Spark.

BYD, for its part, "strongly disagrees" with The Hauge's ruling and is planning to appeal, telling the Wall Street Journal that the Ti7 is "the result of BYD's own independent design work and infringes none of JLR's rights." It added that it will "pursue every legal avenue to demonstrate that this decision ⁠is incorrect.".

#156594. Pondering The Potential Of Plug-In VPP

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1398 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cleantechnica ↗ Open Full Page

Pondering The Potential Of Plug-In VPP

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1398 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I recently discussed the potential of the plug-in VPP from Jackery and Every Electric to transform urban energy storage.
  • It has been revealed that essentially, customers of the plug-in VPP receive a battery, plug it into the wall and their window air conditioner, and connect to Wi-Fi.
  • Sources indicate that both Jackery and Every Electric are collaborating and working to create innovative solutions for customer needs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I recently discussed the potential of the plug-in VPP from Jackery and Every Electric to transform urban energy storage. But the current program could be just the start. The more I discussed it at RE+, the more it started making me thing about where it could go in the future.

It has been revealed that essentially, customers of the plug-in VPP receive a battery, plug it into the wall and their window air conditioner, and connect to Wi-Fi. Then they use AC as they normally would, the VPP shaves off demand peaks on the grid, and the customer gets paid. It is likely the fastest, easiest and cheapest way to implement urban BESS in the US. And regular people living in apartments benefit. You can read more about the plug-in VPP in my previous article for context. Or you can watch the video below.

Sources indicate that both Jackery and Every Electric are collaborating and working to create innovative solutions for customer needs. Plug-in VPP makes the benefits of battery storage accessible to people in apartments. However, the potential could go much farther. Of note, much of what I am discussing here is not available yet. But the plug-in VPP sparked my imagination, and I wanted to expand on what might be possible.

Initially, the system is being deployed in Newly introduced York City, which has a large number of apartments that can be aggregated to create a meaningful amount of combined storage. Of course, the potential can be realized in areas outside of NYC. Every Electric is already looking to expand into the Boston area. There are several other areas where the existing system based on window air conditioners in urban areas could apply, particularly along the Northeast corridor. However, as the program evolves, there is tremendous potential outside of the region.

In Jackery’s home state of California, 4.5 TWh of solar and wind power was curtailed in the first half of 2026. More electricity wasted in six months in one state than many developing countries consume in an entire year. Residential solar often feeds into the grid when it just leads to curtailments elsewhere. Even with recent ESS installations, the Duck Curve is still deepening. If home batteries can help “decapitate the duck,” customers and the utility both stand to benefit. And all that renewable energy presently being wasted can contribute to reducing emissions.

In addition, every Jackery battery can operate as a solar generator, with a DC input. People can simply plug in a solar panel or two to recharge the battery. No additional inverter needed. As it does not send energy back into the grid, it also avoids the cost and complication of traditional grid-tied systems. Sending solar power directly to the battery would avoid having excess solar generation fed into the grid that contributes to overcapacity, deepening the back of the duck curve. Demand response could then come from a battery charged largely from solar, rather than from the grid. As the US is still trying to figure out balcony solar regulations, this would let people enjoy many of the benefits of small scale, plug-and-play solar now. No electricians needed.

Of course, when balcony solar regulations are figured out, Jackery has solutions like the SolarVault3 that I saw at IFA Berlin. Potentially, this system could integrate with point of use battery storage to form a kind of hybrid plug-in system. In the process, solar power could be utilized when it does the most for the grid and offers the greatest potential payback for the customer.

In a recent development, there is also a lot of potential for this concept to work outside of the US. In many parts of the world, most people live in apartments. As the planet warms, world cooling needs recently overtook heating for the first time. As the VPP is monitored via a Wi-Fi connection, there is no need to upgrade to a smart meter to take advantage of the capability. As the storage is already distributed, there is also reduced need to provide the grid upgrades to distribute the energy stored in a large battery during peak energy demand.

According to recent reports, currently, the plug-in VPP is only working with one model of battery in one application. That makes the deployment and scaling of the plug-in VPP easier. Large urban areas offer the clearest path to aggregate the storage needed for a plug-in VPP to work.

Recent findings suggest that however, Jackery has sold over 8 million units over the past 15 years. This has established a level of customer trust and a reputation for reliability. Many of those portable power stations and solar generators can connect to Wi-Fi. That is potentially GWh of deployable storage.

According to recent reports, in addition, portable power stations are very popular now. Many Jackery models are selling out. Preparedness is a major driver. Climate-related disasters amplify the fear and uncertainty. However, the batteries that people are buying to be prepared for emergencies offer far greater potential capability. The more batteries that are out there, the greater the potential.

According to recent reports, as the software and capability of the VPP develop, multiple batteries have the potential to connect to amplify value, even if that capability isn’t being offered yet. Those batteries, in coordination with a VPP, could earn people money. Currently, the system is being run with one battery model, but Jackery offers a wide range of batteries with Wi-Fi connectivity that might be able to participate in the future. Once the program has proven itself with the initial application in urban areas, there is potential for expansion.

As people start earning money, even if they purchased the battery out of preparedness concerns, they would also start to see the broader benefit. When they gain both confidence and financial benefit from battery storage and renewable energy, they will tend to rationalize that benefit. That can lead to a broader shift in mindset. When you try to start with a rational argument, especially when that argument involves added costs, people are less likely to be supportive than if you start with the benefit.

Industry observers note that many of the pieces to make this happen have already existed. People have the ability to program Jackery batteries through the app to charge and discharge during certain parts of the day. This can work with TOU utility plans, where available. But it doesn’t take full advantage of the capabilities of a VPP. Customers do not get full credit for the storage capability. The true innovation comes from putting the pieces together, between the Jackery hardware, Every Electric software and the utility. If one of those pieces of the collaboration was missing, a plug-in VPP wouldn’t have the same potential.

Industry observers note that one of the things that has impressed me about Jackery since I was first introduced to the organization was their focus on solving customer problems. However, to create solutions, they also recognize that collaboration is often necessary. I already saw this with the flexible solar panels of SunBooster at IFA Berlin for balcony solar applications, and then again with Every Electric for plug-in VPP.

I asked Jackery founder and CEO Jack Sun about the value of collaboration in creating an environmentally friendly ecosystem:.

This is also very important, because we have an open model, and we are more willing and more innovative….

It has been revealed that we will actively collaborate with partners in areas such as power chips and more proactively in co-creation. We aim to accelerate the application of their innovations into our solar generator solutions. Our goal is to achieve faster and more efficient solar energy development through joint innovation. The generator can be installed in every household to help more families achieve energy independence more cost-effectively, while also reducing carbon emissions more swiftly.

According to recent reports, this focus on collaboration makes meaningful innovation happen. Just as I speculated here on the potential of plug-in VPP, other people will have their own ideas. Some will be different than this VPP concept. Many will be better ideas than the ideas I can come up with. Having innovative companies like Jackery and Every Electric actively seeking to work with partners creates potential for those ideas to come together. I look forward to seeing what fresh solutions come together next.

#156592. Latest Update: 5 High Horsepower Performance Engines That Are Seemingly Indestructible

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1486 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: 5 High Horsepower Performance Engines That Are Seemingly Indestructible

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1486 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that some engines make a lot of horsepower but are as fleeting as a sunset on a warm summer night.
  • For this list, we picked engines that can take a ton of abuse worry free.
  • Jesse shouldn't have been surprised by the engine under the hood of the mangled Supra Paul Walker's character procured in the first "The Fast and the Furious." All fourth-generation Supras came with 2JZ engines.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that some engines make a lot of horsepower but are as fleeting as a sunset on a warm summer night. The BMW S65 V8 found in the E90-generation M3 that needs rod bearings as preventative maintenance comes to mind, as do Subaru's EJ engines, which are 4-cylinders with a terrible reputation for reliability. But in making some of the best performance engines of all time, some manufacturers have over-built their engines so they are good time for a long time.

For this list, we picked engines that can take a ton of abuse worry free. Some engines, like Toyota's 2JZ-GTE, aren't the most powerful out of the box. But they are under-stressed from the factory, and tuners have more than doubled the engine's output without affecting reliability. Other engines, like the Viper V10, are powerful, reliable, and have an even higher performance ceiling. With that being said, this is not a comprehensive list of brick-house engines by any means. If we missed a motor with a beefcake block, let us know down in the comments.

Jesse shouldn't have been surprised by the engine under the hood of the mangled Supra Paul Walker's character procured in the first "The Fast and the Furious." All fourth-generation Supras came with 2JZ engines. Nonetheless, his excitement was justified. The 2JZ, particularly the factory twin-turbocharged 2JZ-GTE variant, is well known for making big power without sacrificing reliability.

Recent findings suggest that for the U.S. market, the 2JZ-GTE was only found under the hood of the MKIV Supra Turbo, and a little under 7,000 Supra Turbos were sold Stateside. The twin-turbo straight-6 made 320 horsepower from the factory. But it wasn't long before tuners found that the engine was capable of so much more.

The 2JZ's secret sauce largely comes from how its bottom end is constructed. The 2JZ is a closed-deck engine, meaning that the top of the cylinder walls are supported by metal. This, along with the cast iron construction of the 2JZ's engine block, makes the cylinders really strong and able to hold up to a lot of turbo boost. Also, the 2JZ has a forged steel crankshaft. The difference between cast and forged crankshafts comes down to strength and cost. The more common cast crankshaft is cheaper to make, but they are less likely to survive the stresses of an engine outputting substantial horsepower long term. All of this over-engineering means that the 2JZ-GTE can make upward of 700 horsepower without touching the bottom end.

It has been revealed that when Nissan revived the GT-R nameplate for the 2009 model year, it was a revelation. The all-wheel-drive coupe put down acceleration, braking, and road-holding numbers that bested supercars like the Porsche 911 Turbo and Lamborghini LP640 for a fraction of the cost. The center piece of its performance was the twin-turbo 3.8-liter V6 designated VR38DETT. The fresh power plant was rated at 480 horsepower and 430 pound-feet of torque. The 0-to-60 times that the GT-R achieved made the automotive press suspect that Nissan low-balled the twin-turbo V6's output. Indeed, when MotorTrend Channel dyno tested a 2009 GT-R, the outlet found that the factory torque figure was underrated by 40 pound-feet.

Sources indicate that nissan took great care in building the VR38DETT. Each all-aluminum engine was hand assembled by expert craftsmen at Nissan's Yokohama plant in Japan. The VR38 is over square , which means that the engine's construction is more suited for high revs. The GT-R's engine has plasma-coated cylinder bores, which reduce friction and improve cooling. Like the 2JZ-GTE, the VR38 has a robust closed-deck engine block.

Sources indicate that also like the 2JZ, tuners found that the VR38DETT could make a lot more horsepower without a ton of extra work. The engine can safely make around 600 horsepower with the factory turbochargers. Anything above that and you'll be swapping turbos and replacing the connecting rods, which are a known weak point above 650 foot-pounds of torque. The good news is that once the rods are taken care of, the factory block can withstand more than 1,000 hp.

According to recent reports, when Porsche debuted its race-car-for-the-road GT3 in 1999, it equipped its most hardcore 911 with a race-proven engine. The GT3 ditched the standard 911's then-new water-cooled flat-6 engine for a power plant based on the Le Mans-winning 911 GT1, which, in turn, was derived from the engine found in the dominant 962 Group C racer. The engine initially displaced 3.6-liters and output 360 horsepower.

According to recent reports, since it shares the same M96 designation as the engine in the back of the standard 911, enthusiasts call the race-derived engine "Mezger," after Porsche's engine guru Hans Mezger. He was behind the design of the 962 engine, as well as the power plants in the original 911, the 917 race car, and McLaren's 1983-to-1987 F1 entries. In 2000, Porsche strapped a pair of turbochargers to the Mezger for the 911 Turbo, which was good for 415 hp. Porsche used the Mezger in the GT2, GT3, and Turbo until 2013. The ultimate factory Mezger was the turbocharged GT2 RS that made 612 hp. If that's not enough, tuners regularly extract 1,000-plus horsepower out of the Mezger.

Recent findings suggest that over the years, the engine has gained a reputation for its reliability. The reasons why the Mezger flat-6 is bulletproof come down to its construction. First off, the Mezger has a gear-driven intermediate shaft (IMS) with a plain bearing that is always lubricated by engine oil. The unit won't fail catastrophically like the problematic, sealed IMS bearings that plague the M96 and M97 engines found in lesser, contemporary 911s. The Mezger also has a more rigid, reinforced crankcase compared to the standard sixes. And it has individual, pressed-in cylinder liners that are easier to replace than the bores in the standard engine.

Recent findings suggest that what can be remarked that hasn't already been said about Chevrolet's venerable LS V8? It's powerful, compact, and has an abundant aftermarket. The inciting incident for the LS was the 375-horsepower Lotus-designed LT5 V8 in the ZR-1. The good ol' boys on Chevy's internal small-block V8 team were miffed , so they decided to do something that wouldn't have Chevy going to an outside contractor for the 'Vette ever again. The team designed an all-aluminum pushrod V8 , dubbed the LS1, from the ground up. When the LS1 was introduced in the 1997 Corvette, it was only down 30 horsepower compared to the more exotic, quad-cam LT5.

According to recent reports, GM adapted the LS architecture for numerous applications over its 18-year run. As such, LS-architecture V8s were available in a bunch of different flavors, from iron-block 4.8-liter truck motors to all-aluminum 7.0-liter Corvette mills. The most powerful factory variant, the LS9, made 638 hp with help from a 2.3-liter Roots-type supercharger. But crate engines from Chevrolet Performance like the LSX-454R can make over 700 hp without boost.

According to recent reports, the LS in any iteration is a strong base for a performance build. 15 years ago, Hot Rod famously turbocharged a stock-bottom-end 4.8-liter to 1,200 horsepower. Part of the reason for the resilience of that poor 4.8 is that LS engines have six-bolt main bearing caps. The main caps help secure the crankshaft in the block, so, generally speaking, the more bolts that hold the caps, the stronger the bottom end. And it's not just the bottom end. The LS has a valve train that is capable of revving to 7,000 rpm from the factory.

When the Dodge Viper came out in 1992, there was nothing quite like it. It was a 400-horsepower missile that was the the closest thing to a modern Shelby Cobra. The secret to the Viper's prodigious power? An all-aluminum 8.0-liter V10. Lamborghini, a subsidiary of Chrysler at the time, helped  design the V10's aluminum block. Displacement and power figures of the V10 grew throughout the years, with the final Viper ACRs displacing a staggering 8.4 liters and outputting 645 horsepower.

As exotic as an all-aluminum V10 sounds, the Viper engine is known for its reliability, unlike some of the fussy mills in its Italian supercar counterparts. That's not surprising, given the Viper V10 is based on Mopar's LA series V8s. Like the LA engines, the Viper's power plant has two valves per cylinder that are actuated by pushrods. In other words, the engine's architecture is about as simple as it gets.

In a recent development, at more-than-factory horsepower, some Viper V10s are better than others. The V10s built prior to 2000 have forged pistons, which are better able to withstand the stresses from forced induction. Forged pistons didn't reappear until the last generation Viper (2013 to 2017) was blessed with them again. Regardless of which engine you have, suppliers like D.S.S. Racing will be happy to sell you forged pistons that will hold up to boost.

It has been revealed that army states it intends to detonate degraded lead in Iowa town no later than Nov. 24, despite court stay.

Des Moines, IOWA — The Iowa Environmental Council, Sierra Club, and Earthjustice will continue to advocate for accountability from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the U.S. Army in the planned detonation of lead azide in Middletown, Iowa. Early Sunday morning, the groups filed declarations with the court that call out the Army’s inadequate public notice and information, and question the Army’s and EPA’s claims that all alternatives were given appropriate consideration.

The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) filed a statement with the court late on Saturday, Nov. 21, indicating that the Army intends to invoke emergency provisions of the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) to detonate 9,773.5 pounds of lead azide stored at the Iowa Army Ammunitions Plant, without a permit from the EPA. According to the DOJ’s court filings, the Army intends to do so no later than Nov. 24. On Nov. 20, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals granted Earthjustice’s request to put on hold a permit allowing the Army to detonate.

According to recent reports, “People across numerous impacted communities speaking up and demanding accountability is the only reason there was an opportunity to pause and think about better ways to approach the lead azide problem,” stated Earthjustice Attorney Thien Chau. “Yet despite claiming public safety is its top priority and public communication is essential to trust, the Army seemed more concerned over the weekend with finding a way to sidestep the judicial process than on meeting the public’s demands for greater transparency, notice to affected communities, and far stronger protection of people, property, and the environment from serious harm.”.

This emergency is of the Army’s own making. The Army has not publicly provided details about why the lead azide was not disposed of before it became so dangerous. The Army’s own storage and inspection practices allowed a primary explosive to sit until it reportedly degraded to the point that any alternative disposal method is now deemed too dangerous. The lack of transparency raises real questions about the scope and extent of potential impacts.

“The upcoming information from the DOJ indicates that the problem is significantly worse than the Army originally shared. It appears that detonation may be, at this point, the only feasible option due to how long this problem was allowed to persist. The public deserves to know immediately which communities will be impacted and how residents can most effectively protect themselves and mitigate impacts on their health and homes,” said Michael Schmidt, General Counsel for the Iowa Environmental Council.

In a recent development, the Army knew about this stockpile of dangerous munitions waste for years, and it knew since at least March that the material was becoming unstable. Yet, just one week ago, most Iowans — including those directly in the path of a toxic lead plume, the Iowa governor, and key state agencies and officials — were unaware the Army intended to detonate nearly five tons of lead azide.

The environmental groups argue the EPA and Army permitting documents have not demonstrated, nor provided appropriate documentation that all other safer alternatives to mitigate the material were thoroughly explored.

Sources indicate that “The Army has clearly mishandled this situation, and Iowans and residents in our neighboring states deserve a full review of all of the missteps that led us to this point. However, if detonation is now the only option, it is imperative that everyone impacted has access to the full range of testing, mitigation, and remediation resources,” noted Wally Taylor, Attorney and Legal Chair for the Sierra Club Iowa Chapter.

As of 11 a.m. CST on Sunday, Nov. 22, the Army has failed to provide the public with updated weather modeling and mapping showing the path of the lead dust plume, which means people impacted have little time to take precautions to protect their families and homes. The wind patterns have shifted significantly, which means that potential community exposures have likely changed without visible effort by the Army to provide updated information to the public.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COP31 climate talks break down reveals that fossil fuel interests remain a major obstacle to climate action.

The lack of a final text at the end of COP31 demonstrates how far the fossil fuel industry is willing to go to keep its polluting businesses operating, indicates T&E. While the final text of COP28, in 2023, called for ‘transitioning away from fossil fuels in the energy system’, fossil-producing countries have blocked similar language in subsequent COPs despite the growing economic and social costs of climate change.

Recent findings suggest that antony Froggatt, senior director at T&E, said: “In a year marked by record oil prices and extreme temperatures, fossil fuel companies moved to block any agreement calling for a phase-out of oil, gas, and coal. They did so to protect their commercial interests even as solar and wind already power the majority of the grid in countries worldwide, and electric vehicles make up nearly half of newly introduced car sales in the world’s largest auto market.”.

Sources indicate that this is not the end of the international processes, and the Paris Agreement remains in place. The next COP will take place in Ethiopia, and the phase-out of fossil fuels will once again be discussed. In the meantime, the Santa Marta process, which grew out of COP30’s failure to agree on a fossil fuel roadmap, will once again meet, and it is expected that countries representing one-third of the world’s economy will debate and develop practical ways to move away from coal, oil and gas.

Analysis by T&E at the beginning of the week shows that EVs displace five times more oil globally than they did five years ago. Battery-electric vehicles already displace 1.2 million barrels of oil a day and avoid more than 200 Mt of CO2-equivalent a year.

“Petrostates’ chokehold on COP31 underscores the need for the progressive majority to continue pushing for international co-operation and global targets on electrification that can accelerate decarbonisation while improving energy security, air quality and economic prosperity,” added Antony Froggatt.

“The same oil shock that delivered record profits for the oil industry has pushed up costs for the world’s most vulnerable countries, most of which import their fuel. Governments should make the polluter pay. Excess profits should be heavily taxed, and the revenue used to fund electrification and climate resilience where it is needed most,” he concludes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Longevity platform Hone Health nabs $228M to build out offerings" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Hone Health, a physician-led virtual longevity care platform, has raised $228 million.

According to recent reports, the investment is structured as a combination of equity and growth financing. The $28 million series A extension was led by MarcyPen Capital Partners, with participation from Pentland Ventures, Kinship Ventures, Hanwha, Gannet Capital, humbition and Comma Capital. Other angel investors also participated, including the Jonas brothers. The $200 million in growth financing came from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

According to recent reports, hone will use the investment to support a number of expansions. It plans to launch more programming for metabolic health, PMOS, inflammation and immunity, and to launch a physician-supervised peptide program. It will add more diagnostics, including coronary CT angiography and gut microbiome analysis.

Hone also intends to continue building out its AI operating system that brings data together to help personalize care. And it plans to build out clinical trial infrastructure to support pharma partners.

“Longevity is thought of as this super exotic thing. […] I actually think longevity is now becoming primary care,” Saad Alam, co-founder and CEO of Hone, told Fierce Healthcare.

In a recent development, it costs $65 to test for 70 biomarkers with Hone, followed by a clinician consult with the option to add more diagnostics. Labs, health history, symptoms and medications are run through its AI, which then gives providers treatment recommendations. Hone can keep adding additional diagnostics and medications, per Alam, “and the AI gets smarter as we get more patients into that system.”.

Additionally, Hone is publicly announcing Hone Black, a fresh concierge longevity membership that has operated in stealth for a select group of patients for the past year. It combines diagnostics on over 1,600 health markers with ongoing medical care from physicians. Offerings include prescriptions, supplements, peptides and lifestyle guidance, plus exosome and stem cell therapies.

Alam founded the manufacturer after experiencing a shift in his health at 35 years old, including mental health problems, depression and weight gain. His doctor was initially of little help. It took Alam a year to find out he had low testosterone, and after treatment, he finally felt back on track. That experience, along with his father dying from kidney disease and his mother going through early menopause, opened his eyes to the longevity space.

Industry observers note that “This whole concept of longevity is going to be one of the single greatest problems I can dedicate my life to solving,” Alam realized at the time. He experimented with everything, from peptides to cold plunges to meditation.

It has been revealed that hone is a subsidiary of Time Therapeutics, which aims to support production of drugs that help people live longer. Alam, who started his career doing market research at Eli Lilly, knew clinical trials are expensive and inaccessible. He wanted to create a company that could help commercialize drugs. The first step to that is Hone, or a DTC virtual care company that can capture longitudinal data on patients. The next phase will be publishing research. Finally, Hone will look to partner with pharma to get drugs to market faster.

The company has been providing care for five years, treating about 200,000 patients to date. It requires patients to have a physician and get bloodwork every 90 days in order to get medication refills. Members can contact their clinician between sessions as needed.

“We make sure, for the most part, that you are doing bloodwork and talking to a physician, a real conversation with a physician, in order to get prescribed medication,” Alam said.

It isn’t about overprescribing medications. It’s about finding the most personalized protocol for each patient. “The companies that have—no pun intended—longevity are the ones that are going to figure out how to reduce the number of medications somebody might need,” Alam said.

Hone began with hormone therapy, then moved into longevity care with biomarker analysis and women’s health. Two months ago, Hone’s offerings for women surpassed offerings for men in terms of net newly introduced members. It soon aims to run clinical trials on poly-chronic patients as well to help determine the right drug at the right time. Hone crossed $100 million in revenue in 2025, per Alam, and is on track to double this year.

It has been revealed that “When I started goop, wellness was a niche conversation,” Gwyneth Paltrow, founder and CEO of goop and co-founder of Kinship Ventures, said in a press release. “Today, it’s one of the biggest categories in the world, and the next step is bringing real health and wellness to the masses, not just the few. Saad has built Hone to do exactly that, with serious science and at real scale. That’s why Kinship invested, and we could not be more excited about what’s ahead.”.

Hone will soon offer 14 longevity care categories, which Alam argues is akin to primary care. He estimates that Hone only refers to in-person care about 10% of the time, usually for higher-acuity conditions. Some Hone patients are already healthy; most are sick and willing to pay out of pocket because the current system has been inadequate in solving their health needs, per Alam.

It has been revealed that “This is just the beginning of not only a way but a complete change in the way that medicine is practiced,” Alam stated. “A lot of other companies are what I’ll call pill mills, and where we’ve really focused—our energy is making sure that we go through the more difficult work of managing the long-term health of our patients.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No championship fight is ever over until it's over. Marc Marquez clinched the 2026 MotoGP World Championship on Sunday after finishing eighth at the Portuguese Grand Prix. The Spaniard overcame a record 106-point deficit to win his eighth MotoGP title and his tenth world championship across all Grand Prix classes. Marquez's eighth top-class crown ties in the record books with Giacomo Agostini, the sport's greatest of all time. In true MotoGP fashion, the post-race championship fits the moment's monumental nature.

According to recent reports, if it weren't for his history-making triumph, it would have been a weekend at Portimão to forget for Marquez. He had the opportunity to win the championship during Saturday's sprint race, but dramatically pushed the title fight to Sunday. In damp conditions, Marquez was riding in third with only a lap and a half to go when his factory Ducati slid out from under him at Turn 7. He and his bike went off into the gravel. Thankfully for his title hopes, the Spaniard was fine. Seeing how his coronation could be canceled, Marquez took no chances during the feature. He bolted to the lead at the start, then cruised home.

Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi swept the weekend in Portugal, winning the sprint and feature races from pole. However, eighth place was enough for Marquez to win the title. According to Motorsport.com, he noted post-race. "Yesterday was a massive warning, so today I said 'f*** off' [to] the race. I didn't care about the result. I just I wanted to close the championship.".

Recent findings suggest that relief and ecstasy overcame Marquez after he crossed the finish line and was mobbed by his fellow competitors, trackside marshals and Ducati personnel. As is MotoGP tradition, there was an elaborate celebration for the champion. He climbed atop a platform to don a gold-trimmed jersey in front of his adoring fans, picking up a microphone to thank them. Marquez then trotted over to a massive videoboard to watch a crash-filled career highlight reel, which featured Valentino Rossi's infamous 2015 kick.

The celebration's finale saw Marquez climb a ten-step staircase, recognizing his ten world championships, with the shadow of a goat behind him. At the summit, Agostini emerged from a hidden door to present Marquez with a golden helmet. He then rode his Ducati to the championship stage with a Spanish flag in hand, screaming his lungs out.

Sunday was arguably the capstone moment of Marquez's career. While the 33-year-old signed a two-year extension to remain at Ducati through the 2028 season, no one can guarantee that he will win another world championship. He was nearly cut short after breaking his arm in 2020. The allure of a tenth world title has proven to be a specter that haunts MotoGP's recent greats. His long-time rival Valentino Rossi spent a dozen years trying to win his tenth world title. Despite retiring in 2021, the legendary Italian still can't let go of his 2015 title fight and feud with Marquez.

Tech Report: Barcelona Is Suffering From The Hydrogen Transport Death Spiral

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (900 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that on November 21, Barcelona had at least 23 of its 46 hydrogen buses out of service because the plant supplying them had stopped producing fuel.
  • In a recent development, the problem runs through a single industrial fuel supply.
  • It has been revealed that la Vanguardia connected the Barcelona stoppage with Cummins’ recommendation that customers stop using affected electrolysers following a safety review.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on November 21, Barcelona had at least 23 of its 46 hydrogen buses out of service because the plant supplying them had stopped producing fuel. Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) reported a 2.5% to 3.8% reduction in scheduled bus service, with waits on some routes rising from seven to nine minutes. The buses were available to carry passengers. The hydrogen was not. ARA and La Vanguardia reported the disruption.

In a recent development, the problem runs through a single industrial fuel supply. TMB has a ten-year, €14.5 million hydrogen contract with Iberdrola. Alternative deliveries from Tarragona have fallen short, disrupted by industrial action and restrictions on hydrogen transport. The contract provides for compensation when fuel is not delivered. It cannot make up the missed service.

It has been revealed that la Vanguardia connected the Barcelona stoppage with Cummins’ recommendation that customers stop using affected electrolysers following a safety review. Iberdrola cited a valve-system problem at the plant. Cummins’ November quarterly filing confirmed the September HyLYZER stop-use recommendation and said no formal recall had been initiated. TMB now has to assess the price of safely restarting fuel production and the reliability of the system it would be restarting.

Barcelona has not decided to retire the hydrogen buses. But the agency has a more key decision than repairing a plant: whether it should commit public money to keeping this fuel system in service for the remainder of the buses’ lives. Other European cities have faced that choice and walked away.

It has been revealed that aberdeen paid approximately £13.9 million for 25 hydrogen double-deckers that entered service in 2021. Hydrogen supply problems stranded the fleet in July 2024. After prolonged efforts to restore the operation, the city decided in February 2026 to dispose of the buses. A proposed sale would bring in £30,000 each for 23 buses going to First Bus and £63,000 each for two going to GeoPura. The total expected proceeds are £816,000, just 5.9% of the original vehicle expenditure. My September Aberdeen resale assessment examined the proposed terms and the conversion economics. First Bus has also considered battery-electric conversion.

In a recent development, liverpool chose conversion. Ten of its 20 hydrogen buses had never carried passengers; the other ten had completed only 450 passenger-carrying journeys. In December 2025 the Liverpool City Region Combined Authority decided to convert all 20 to battery-electric operation, with the supplier covering the conversion costs. The buses had years of potential mechanical life, but the hydrogen supply arrangements had not delivered a usable transport service.

A hydrogen bus can become an uneconomic asset long before it wears out. Refuelling plants, fuel deliveries, maintenance specialists, software, fuel-cell modules and replacement parts have to remain available. As hydrogen fleets retire and fresh orders thin out, each remaining operator has fewer other customers sharing those support costs. Rising costs and uncertain service then encourage another operator to exit. That is the hydrogen transport death spiral. Battery-electric buses draw on a much larger manufacturing, charging and maintenance market.

The pressures already extend through the supply chain. Cummins has stopped seeking new commercial electrolyser business while customers contend with its HyLYZER stop-use recommendation. Quantron’s insolvency disrupted confidence in specialist vehicle support. Alstom acquired Cummins’ relevant rail fuel-cell operations to retain the staff and expertise needed to fulfil long-term contracts. Each case transfers more risk to organizations that have already bought hydrogen equipment.

In a recent development, new Flyer still sells hydrogen buses, but the North American order book is thin. Publicly identified hydrogen-bus orders numbered 288 in 2023, 96 in 2024 and no more than 45 gross in 2025, with about 15 in a stricter reconstruction. Another 38 buses appear in 2026 procurement decisions across differing approval stages. These are small volumes for a specialist vehicle line that needs engineering, spares and continuing product development.

According to recent reports, ballard is still developing bus fuel cells. Its November 5 Solaris announcement describes a new engine entering series production. Its GeoPura acquisition also shifts business attention toward integrated power systems and recurring energy-service revenue. My Ballard–New Flyer framework assessment found that the March agreement covering 500 modules is not an order for 500 buses. For a transit operator, the crucial test is a binding, affordable commitment to parts, diagnostics and maintenance throughout the vehicles’ remaining service lives.

TMB should compare the cost of safely restarting the hydrogen plant and running the buses with the cost of delivering the same passenger service through replacement vehicles. That includes the repair bill, future fuel contracts, station maintenance, spare parts, service interruptions, replacement buses, depot charging and any temporary vehicles required to keep routes operating. TMB already runs battery-electric buses and has local operating data to test a replacement proposal.

Industry observers note that A modest repair may justify running the existing hydrogen buses while alternatives are prepared. A major refurbishment, fresh fuel commitments and another decade of specialist support are a different investment. Aberdeen chose disposal. Liverpool chose conversion. Barcelona needs to decide what delivers dependable bus service at the lowest credible forward cost, without treating the original hydrogen spending as money it can recover.

In a recent development, my full TFIE Strategy Briefing assessment examines the Barcelona interruption, the Aberdeen and Liverpool exits, and the contracting support market. The paid section sets out how transit boards can compare restarting, bridging and retiring an existing hydrogen fleet.

#156581. What Happens To The Cars A Dealership Can't Sell?

What Happens To The Cars A Dealership Can't Sell?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (754 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Americans buy about 16 million latest cars every year, barring the occasional economic upheaval or global pandemic.
  • Industry observers note that used cars can sit around, too.
  • It has been revealed that there wasn't always a reason for what made a slow seller.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Americans buy about 16 million latest cars every year, barring the occasional economic upheaval or global pandemic. Yet, that heady number doesn't take into account that not every car sells like manufacturers and dealers hope. Some models languish on lots for months or even years. One of the first things dealers try is offering customers a discount. At the dealership where I sold new and used cars, the bosses would also offer incentives to salespeople to move cars that just couldn't gain traction. More aggressive tactics like converting the car into a service loaner or demonstrator could also come into play. Then, surrender might come in the form of trading the car to another dealer or sending the vehicle to a wholesale auction. In case you're wondering, bidding at these dealer-only auctions usually requires a license.

Industry observers note that used cars can sit around, too. What's considered a slow seller? It varies by company, but many dealers consider 60 to 90 days on the lot long enough for a car to count as aged inventory. At my dealership, management started to get anxious at the 60-day mark. Why? Because most dealers don't own their inventories outright. The cars you see on the lot and in storage yards are financed. It's called floorplanning, which contributes a significant amount to the overhead. Last year, the average floorplan costs for a newly introduced car were about $237 per month. That amount quickly eats into profits as the months accumulate.

It has been revealed that there wasn't always a reason for what made a slow seller. Sometimes, it was the color (the used car manager was prohibited from buying anything brown) or the lack of a particular option. Pricing was always a factor. An overpriced, unpopular model is a direct cause of crickets chirping.

Money has a way of motivating customers and salespeople when it comes to old inventory. Sometimes, extra discounts or a better trade-in valuation is all it takes. In my selling days, management would also tack on bonuses on aged units. If someone came in hell-bent on the best deal possible and was less focused on the car (yes, those buyers exist), I would steer them toward these options. It was usually a win for everyone.

Yet, money can't fix everything. In these situations, the choice could involve taking the problematic latest car out of inventory and doing something else with it. The typical routes are making the car a service loaner or letting a manager drive it as a demonstrator. After a time, the vehicle may then make its way back to the lot, but sometimes on the used car side of the business. Demonstrator units typically go up for sale before the odometer hits 3,000 miles. It may be sold as new if it was never registered, but the high-for-a-new-car mileage usually comes with a disclosure and a discount.

Recent findings suggest that at the dealership I worked at, the company also had a thriving car rental division (they were stingy with loaner cars), so it wasn't unusual to see older units positioned there. In theory, any of these steps could be taken with slow-selling used cars, but from my experience, dealers often use newer models for loaners, demonstrators, or rentals.

Industry observers note that if discounts and incentives can't move older upcoming inventory and changing over to loaners isn't practical, dealers use other measures to get the offending car off the lot. Dealers trade vehicles with each other. It's a common practice among franchised dealers. A slow-seller in one market might be the right model for another. The transaction could be a vehicle swap with a cash payment for any difference in value, or the other dealer will just make an outright purchase. My dealership had relationships with several other same-brand retailers outside our immediate trading area.

Industry observers note that wholesale auctions are the last-resort inventory disposal method. At this point, the dealership has decided to cut its losses. However, the bleeding can get worse. There are costs to bring a car to auction (fees and transportation costs). Also, an auction may not fetch a satisfactory price. It can be a gamble.

Specialized auctions for franchised dealers from the same brand also exist. Fresh cars can go to auction, too. Minnesota statute, for example, allows dealers in that state to auction new vehicles. For used cars, outlets like Manheim and Openlane let dealers offload unsuccessful inventory. ADESA, which Carvana bought a few years ago, is another.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ahmedabad, India — Adani Cement, part of the Adani Portfolio and one of India’s leading building materials solutions providers, flagged off Heavy-Duty Electric Trucks at its Sanghi Plant in Gujarat. This is the first-ever deployment of EV trucks by Adani Cement and a defining milestone in the tech giant’s sustainability and green logistics journey.

Mr. Vinod Bahety, CEO of Cement Business, Adani Group, stated, “The deployment at Sanghi is just the beginning. We have identified multiple routes across India for EV-based transport of clinker and cement. Every truck we electrify reduces our carbon footprint and insulates our logistics cost base from diesel price volatility. This is smart sustainability—it benefits the people, the planet, and the balance sheet. This is our commitment in action—to build a greener, more competitive cement company that serves India’s growth while protecting its future.”.

According to recent reports, the economic case for heavy-duty EV trucks in India’s cement sector has reached a structural tipping point. Over the past decade, diesel prices rose 60%, while Li-ion battery pack costs fell by approximately 70% and solar tariffs declined 47%.

Diesel trucks emit approximately 0.7375 kg CO₂ per km and when powered by renewable energy, EV trucks can eliminate up to 100% of these freight emissions, making logistics electrification a powerful lever for Scope 3 decarbonization. Adani Cement’s 410-truck fleet is projected to reduce over 25,000 tonnes of CO₂ annually, displacing the equivalent of 11 million litres of diesel per year, with prepares to expand across additional routes and plants.

According to recent reports, india is the world’s second-largest cement producer, and the movement of limestone, clinker, and finished cement across vast supply chains is an essential, but carbon-intensive, part of the sector’s operations. Adani Cement’s EV fleet deployment addresses both the cost and climate dimensions of this challenge directly.
